openings.claim: Checking each open envelope against its assigned sample before closure, then pencilling the pattern on its exterior, could resist omissions and distribution mix-ups for participants and the two assemblers. No benefit has been demonstrated.
openings.delta: Keep the shared tagged trays. One volunteer picks into an open envelope; the other verifies quantities and dimensions against the assigned sample, corrects omissions, marks the pattern and closes it. Exchange roles between batches. Replace the deferred contents check with this integrated check.
openings.prediction: With the same pattern mixture, verification will intercept missing items before closure and exterior labels will prevent assignment exchanges. The eventual target remains 60 complete, pattern-matched kits within 90 minutes, with at most one correction at distribution; throughput is unproven.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is local picking supplies beside each assembler with deferred checking. If shared-tray interference drives omissions, local picking will reduce initial omissions without an integrated checker, whereas the proposed shared-tray process will retain picking errors and may exceed the time budget.
openings.defeat: When comparison batches contain errors, integrated checking leaves as many residual omissions as deferred checking, or a full run exceeds 90 minutes or needs more than one distribution correction. Mislabelled patterns also defeat the assignment claim.
openings.probe: Within a single 90-minute cap, the same two volunteers assemble two matched twelve-kit batches using the same pattern mixture: incumbent deferred checking and proposed integrated checking. Record initial omissions, corrections, residual omissions, exterior assignment errors and elapsed time including checks. Use only existing table space, envelopes, pencils, samples, trays and tally sheets; stop before exceeding the cap. A zero-error comparison is inconclusive. A later full 60-kit run is necessary to test the workshop target.
assumptions: Fit evaluates the bounded proposed probe; the eventual 60-kit intervention remains unproven.
Existing samples accurately specify each pattern's quantities and dimensions.
Two matching twelve-kit batches can be constituted from existing supplies; verify stock before allocating them.
Integrated verification is fast enough for the eventual target; the probe measures this rather than presuming it.
